order: Grant the agents that carry out work the git permissions they need to complete orders that call for committing and pushing. Subagents cannot accept authorization relayed through a work order the way a native prompt can, so without an explicit settings-level grant they are denied git commit and git push even when the user has ordered the work. Update the installer to merge the three relevant git command patterns into the allow list in the project's settings file, merging idempotently so re-running the installer does not duplicate entries or clobber anything already present. Update the uninstaller to remove exactly those three grants and nothing else the user may have added since. Keep the existing guard-hook restriction that bars the Director itself from running shell commands intact, so the new grants extend only to the agents doing the work, not to the Director.
claims: The installer now merges the three git command permissions into the allow list idempotently, and the uninstaller removes exactly those grants. The Director remains barred from shell commands by the existing guard hook, so the change empowers only the agents carrying out work orders, not the Director itself.
